correct_completion: the host closed the door and turned off the lights.
full_sentence: The last guest having left, the host closed the door and turned off the lights.
acceptable_variants: the host finally locked up for the night.
the host turned off the lights and went to bed.

options.text: so the host closed the door.
options.why_wrong: Adding 'so' turns the sentence into a cause-effect link; an absolute clause expresses background circumstance without a linking word.

options.text: the host was closing the door.
options.why_wrong: The continuous form describes an action in progress, but the perfect participle 'having left' signals an action completed before the main clause.

options.text: the host closed the door and turned off the lights.
and the host, closing the door.
options.why_wrong: This has no finite main clause, so the participle 'closing' cannot stand alone as the predicate.

grammar_focus: Absolute participle clauses with a perfect participle
explanation: The perfect participle clause 'having left' has its own implied subject, 'the last guest', so the main clause needs a new subject, 'the host'. Learners often add a linking word or repeat a finite verb pattern, which breaks the structure.
translation: Gdy ostatni gość już wyszedł, gospodarz zamknął drzwi i zgasił światła.
